---
author: indexwc team
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
params:
  common: species name
  used_only: true
title: "`r stringr::str_to_sentence(params$common)`"
header-includes:
  - \usepackage[acronym]{glossaries}
  - \glsdisablehyper
  - \loadglsentries{indexwc_glossaries.tex}
bibliography: indexwc.bib
output:
  pdf_document:
    keep_md: true
---

```{r setup, echo = FALSE, warnings = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Load package helpers and libraries used to assemble and render the report.
library(devtools)
library(dplyr)
library(glue)
library(knitr)
library(nwfscSurvey)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(xfun)
load_all()
# Keep the generated report focused on its text, without routine chunk output.
options(knitr.duplicate.label = "allow")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
# Select this species' configurations, optionally including unused alternatives.
configuration <- read.csv(
  #file = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pfmc-assessments/indexwc/main/data-raw/configuration.csv"
  file = here::here("data-raw/configuration.csv") # using local file because branch is not yet merged 
) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    species == params$common,
    !params$used_only | used
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Derive display labels without evaluating candidate family constructors.
    distribution = gsub("^.*::", "", family),
    distribution = gsub("\\(.*$", "", distribution),
    distribution = sub("^delta_", "", distribution),
    distribution = gsub("_mix$", " mixture", distribution),
    distribution = gsub("^tweedie$", "Tweedie", distribution),
    # Map internal survey names to glossary labels used in section headings.
    text_survey = dplyr::case_when(
      source == "NWFSC.Combo" ~ "s-wcgbt",
      source == "Triennial" ~ "s-tri",
      source == "AFSC.Slope" ~ "s-aslope",
      source == "NWFSC.Slope" ~ "s-nwslope",
      TRUE ~ "unknown survey"
    ),
    # Convert spatial-model settings into report-ready descriptions.
    text_spatiotemporal = dplyr::case_when(
      spatiotemporal1 == "iid" & spatiotemporal2 == "iid" ~
        "Spatial and spatiotemporal variation were included in the encounter probability and the positive catch rate model.",
      spatiotemporal1 == "off" & spatiotemporal2 == "iid" ~
        "Spatial and spatiotemporal variation were included in the positive catch rate model but only spatial variation was included in the encounter probability.",
      spatiotemporal1 == "iid" & spatiotemporal2 == "off" ~
        "Spatial and spatiotemporal variation were included in the encounter probability but only spatial variation was included in the positive catch rate model.",
      spatiotemporal1 == "off" & spatiotemporal2 == "off" ~
        "Spatiotemporal variation was not included in either the encounter probability nor the positive catch rate model (but spatial variation was included in both models)."
    )
  )
# Number multiple configurations from one survey so their sections are distinguishable.
configuration <- configuration |>
  # Group survey sections together while retaining configuration order within each source.
  dplyr::arrange(source) |>
  dplyr::group_by(source) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    text_survey_option = if (dplyr::n() > 1) {
      paste0(" (Option ", dplyr::row_number(), ")")
    } else {
      rep("", dplyr::n())
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r setup-asis, include=FALSE}
# Pass generated child-document lines through as Markdown in the parent report.
knit_engines$set(asis = function(options) {
  # if (options$echo && options$eval)
  paste(options$code, collapse = ' ')
})
```

## Survey indices of abundance

Geostatistical models of biomass density were fit to survey data using the R package \gls{sdmtmb} [@Anderson:2022:SRP].
These models can account for latent spatial factors with a constant spatial Gaussian Markov random
field (GRMF) and spatiotemporal deviations as independent draws from the GRMF [@thorson_geostatistical_2015]. A range of alternative distributions were investigated. Results are only shown for
the distribution that led to the best model diagnostics, e.g., similar
distributions of theoretical normal quantiles and model quantiles, high
precision, lack of extreme predictions that are incompatible with the life
history, and low \gls{aic}. Estimates of biomass from this best model were
predicted using a grid based on available survey locations. The {indexwc} R 
package [@johnson_indexwc_2025] was used to conduct the analysis and code to
reproduce the analysis is available at
https://pfmc-assessments.github.io/indexwc/.

```{r, knit-child, results='asis'}
# Share fetched survey data across the configuration rows rendered below.
data_cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

# Render each configuration in its own child-document environment.
knit_child_with_params <- function(data) {
  env_local <- new.env()
  assign("species", data[["species"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("fxn", data[["fxn"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("source", data[["source"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("text_survey_option", data[["text_survey_option"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("data_cache", data_cache, envir = env_local)
  assign("family", data[["family"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("formula", data[["formula"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("min_depth", data[["min_depth"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("max_depth", data[["max_depth"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("min_latitude", data[["min_latitude"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("max_latitude", data[["max_latitude"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("min_year", data[["min_year"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("max_year", data[["max_year"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("anisotropy", data[["anisotropy"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("n_knots", data[["knots"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("distribution", data[["distribution"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("text_survey", data[["text_survey"]], envir = env_local)
  assign("text_spatiotemporal", data[["text_spatiotemporal"]], envir = env_local)
  # Knit the child document using this row's configuration values.
  knitr::knit_child(
    "child.Rmd",
    envir = env_local,
    quiet = TRUE
  )
}

# Nest each configuration row separately, then concatenate the rendered sections.
res <- configuration |>
    dplyr::group_nest(dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::pull(data) |>
    purrr::map(.f = knit_child_with_params)

cat(unlist(res), sep = '\n')
```
